Would these ops do the same on the current revision?

Source: R/sections.R
rebase_check.Rd

A draft is a scenario under a base revision, and its ops are approved by replaying them on the current revision, so approved revisions stay one chain. That is safe when the rows the ops touch are the same on both plans. This finds the rows where they are not.

Usage

rebase_check(base, current, ops)

Arguments

base

The plan the ops were written against: the draft's parent.

current

The plan they would be replayed on: normally the current approved revision. Must share base's grain.

ops

The ops, in any form ops_within() takes – including the draft's own @edits record.

Value

A data frame with one row per op side and row that differs:

op, side

As in ops_within().

row

The row's key: line_item() at the full grain.

issue

"changed", "base only" or "current only".

columns

For "changed", the columns that differ, joined with ", "; NA otherwise.

base_spend, current_spend

The row's planned spend on each plan as the op finds it; NA where the op does not select it.

Details

The ops are resolved on both plans, in order, as build_scenario() would apply them. For each op side, the rows it selects on base are compared with the rows it selects on current: a row selected on one and not the other is reported, and so is a row selected on both whose planned_spend, spend bounds (bound_cols()) or flight columns (flight_cols()) differ. Those are the facts an op's arithmetic reads – a delta spreads by the group's spend, a transfer routes around its bounds, money moved into an empty line spreads by its flight days – so zero rows means replaying the ops on current does to those rows what it did on base.

Rows the ops do not touch may differ freely: a sibling section approved in between is not a conflict. An add selects nothing, so it is compared only through the ops after it. An op that cannot be applied to one of the plans at all – its target is gone – is an error naming the plan, since replaying it there would fail the same way.

See also

ops_within(), current_approved()

Examples

base <- media_plan_from_df(
  data.frame(week = as.Date("2026-07-06"),
             channel = c("TV", "TV", "Search", "Social"),
             partner = c("NBC", "ESPN", "Google", "Meta"),
             planned_spend = c(50, 30, 40, 40)),
  grain = c("channel", "partner"), time = "week", name = "Rev 1"
)
draft <- op_transfer(10, from = list(partner = "NBC"),
                     to = list(partner = "ESPN"))

# Search was cut in the meantime: no conflict with a TV draft
current <- build_scenario(base, op_scale(0.5, list(channel = "Search")),
                          name = "Rev 2")
rebase_check(base, current, draft)
#> [1] op            side          row           issue         columns      
#> [6] base_spend    current_spend
#> <0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)

# NBC was cut: the draft's source is not what it was
current <- build_scenario(base, op_scale(0.5, list(partner = "NBC")),
                          name = "Rev 2")
rebase_check(base, current, draft)
#>   op side                   row   issue       columns base_spend current_spend
#> 1  1 from TV | NBC | 2026-07-06 changed planned_spend         50            25
